Credible regions of location surfaces

Source: R/credible_region.R
credible_region.Rd

For each animal and bin, the smallest set of cells that holds level of the probability of a location surface: the cells where the animal most probably was, and how large that area is.

Usage

credible_region(surface, level = 0.95, raster = FALSE)

Arguments

surface

A location surface from location_surface().

level

Share of the probability the region holds, above 0 and at most the surface's kept mass.

raster

If TRUE, return a terra raster with one layer per animal and bin, holding each cell's probability inside the region and NA outside it, instead of the table.

Value

A data frame of class "credible_region" with the columns animal_id, bin_start, cell and prob, one row per cell in a region, and the attribute summary: one row per animal and bin with n_cells, area_m2 and mass, the probability the region holds. With raster = TRUE, a SpatRaster.

Details

Cells enter in order of probability until their sum reaches level; ties go to the cell listed first. A surface stores only the cells that hold its kept mass (0.999 by default), so level cannot exceed it. A surface cut down by subsetting may store less than level in some bins; their regions then hold every stored cell, and a warning gives their number.

The area is the number of cells times the cell area of the surface's grid, in square metres; on a longitude-latitude grid each cell's own area is summed.

See also

location_surface()

Examples

tif <- system.file("extdata", "stoney_depth.tif", package = "detfield")
grid <- terra::rast(tif)
# Beyond 2 km the Stoney curve is below 0.001 at every receiver; leaving
# those pairs out keeps the example quick.
dist <- water_distances(grid, stoney_track$receivers,
                        max_distance = 2000)
model <- de_logistic(d50 = c(250, 750), d05 = c(500, 1500), depth = c(1, 35))
field <- de_field(dist, de_model(model, sigma = list(station_hour = 0)))
#> 194 of 7,669 receiver-cell pairs with p >= 0.05 have land on the
#>   straight line between them; with blocked = 0 the curve is read on
#>   them as if the line were clear. See `blocked` in ?de_model.
counts <- bin_detections(stoney_track$detections, stoney_track$receivers,
                         stoney_track$tags)
surface <- location_surface(counts, field)
region <- credible_region(surface, level = 0.95)
attr(region, "summary")
